title: Variance and deterministic decision-tree depth
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function that assigns positive probability to every element of $\Omega$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose the real vector space of functions on $\Omega$ has a basis indexed by $\iota$ whose distinguished vector is the constant-one function and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For any $n\ge 0$ and any function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$ and not constant, its variance under the product distribution $\pi^n$, divided by its deterministic decision-tree depth, is at most its maximum coordinate influence.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function with full support
$\iota$ is finite and nonempty and has decidable equality
There is a real basis of functions on $\Omega$ indexed by $\iota$
The distinguished basis vector is constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
